headline: Accepted no contest pleas and fines for Mangos Hookah Lounge and Picos; summons issued to Acruz Events and Art Gallery.
summary: Several event, sign, and waste hauler licenses were approved, along with outdoor seating at 99 India Street. Mangos Hookah Lounge and Picos Restaurant & Hookah Lounge had pleas accepted and fines set, and Picos will be suspended for one day on August 7, 2026. Acruz Events and Art Gallery was summoned to a formal hearing on September 10, 2026.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 22, 2026 meeting as prepared by the Clerk.
Approved the Consent Agenda on a unanimous voice vote.
Approved a license for a car show at 45 Alden Street on August 15, 2026, on a unanimous voice vote.
Approved a license for the Rhode Island Lights Festival at Centreville Bank Stadium, November 27, 2026 through January 3, 2027, on a unanimous voice vote.
Approved the sign permit renewal for Minuteman Press at 805 Central Ave. on a unanimous voice vote.
Approved the waste hauler renewal for Rambone Disposal Service on a unanimous voice vote.
Approved a license and one-day liquor license expansion for the Jacques 126th Anniversary Celebration at 816 Main Street on August 15, 2026, on a unanimous voice vote.
Approved outdoor seating expansion for Pawtucket Patriot Bar & Grill at 99 India St. on a unanimous voice vote.
Approved the name change of Pawtucket Patriot Bar and Grill to Pawtucket Patriot Bar & BBQ on a unanimous voice vote.
Continued the public hearing and postponed the auto repair shop application for Correia Auto Repair to September 10, 2026.
Rescheduled the hearing on the Tiki's Auto Sales Annex license to September 10, 2026, on a unanimous voice vote.
Rescheduled the formal hearing on the Harmony kennel renewal to September 10, 2026, on a unanimous voice vote.
Postponed the Harmony kennel renewal again, to September 10, 2026, on a unanimous voice vote.
Accepted the no contest plea from Mangos Hookah Lounge and stayed a $500 fine for 120 days.
Placed on file a communication from Steven Knapp about noise from an event at Picos.
Accepted the no contest plea from Picos Restaurant & Hookah Lounge, ordered a $500 fine paid within 45 days, and a one-day license suspension on August 7, 2026.
Placed on file a police communication about a large disorderly crowd at 249 Main Street.
Approved issuing a summons to Acruz Events and Art Gallery to appear at a formal hearing on September 10, 2026.

358 
Pawtucket Board of License Commissioners 
August 5, 2026 
 
A regular session of the Pawtucket Board of License Commissioners was held Wednesday, 
August 5, 2026, at 6:52 p.m., in the Temporary City Council Chambers, 2nd floor, 100 Freight 
Street, Pawtucket, RI. 
 
Present – President Mercer; Councilors Araujo, Coderre, Moran, Moreno, Rubio, Stachowiak 
and Wildenhain. 
 
Absent – Councilor Gregor. 
 
Chairperson Mercer presided.  
 
 
The reading of the records of July 22 , 2026 was dispensed with and the records were 
APPROVED as prepared by the Clerk. 
 
 
Upon motion made by Councilor Araujo, seconded by Councilor  Moreno, the *Consent 
Agenda was APPROVED, on a unanimous voice vote. 
 
 
*THE FOLLOWING PETITION S FOR LICENSE WERE APPROVED ON A 
UNANIMOUS VOICE VOTE: 
 
A. ENTERTAINMENT – 
 
Petition of Phillip Marques , for license to conduct a Car Show at 45 Alden Street, on 
Saturday, August 15, 2026, from 3:00 p.m. until 6:00 p.m. LIC#EVT-26-72 
 
B.  ENTERTAINMENT –  
 
Petition of Centerville Bank Stadium  at Tidewater Landing for  a license to conduct 
 Rhode Island Lights Festival at Centreville Bank Stadium  (winter wonderland immersive 
walk through light experience) beginning Friday, November 27, 2026 through Sunday, 
January 3, 2027.   7-days per week, Sundays -Thursdays 5:00 p.m. - 9:00 p.m.; Fridays -
Saturdays 5:00 p.m.-10:00 p.m. LIC#EVT-26-71 
 
SIGN PERMIT Renewal –  
 
Minuteman Press (KS Designs LLC) 805 Central Ave. (1) LIC#SGN-24-3 
 
WASTE HAULER Renewal –  
 
Rambone Disposal Service (Rambone Disposal Service, Inc.) 2153 Plainfiel d Pike, Johnston, 
RI (2) LIC#WST-24-7 
 
 
THE FOLLOWING PETITION FOR LICENSE S WAS APPROVED ON A UNANIMOUS 
VOICE VOTE: 
 
ENTERTAINMENT & EXPANSION OF PREMISE (One Day) –  
 
Petition of Societe Jacques Cartier Cercle No. 4 , for license to conduct the Jacques 126 th 
Anniversary Celebration and for a one-day expansion of their Class D Liquor License to serve 
food and alcoholic beverages at 816 Main Street, (outdoors and indoors) on Saturday, August 
15, 2026, from 11:00 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. LIC#EVT-26-69 
 
Councilor Araujo recused himself on the petition from Societe Jacques Cartier Cercle No. 4, 
based on his statement, “Member of the Club.” (Report Filed)
359 
Pawtucket Board of License Commissioners 
August 5, 2026 
 
A PUBLIC HEARING  FOR EXPANSION OF PREMISE , WHICH WAS ADVERTISED 
FOR A HEARING AT THIS TIME,  WAS TAKEN UP: 
 
CLASS B (VICTUALLER) Expansion of premise to include outdoor seating - 
 
Pawtucket Patriot Bar & Grill (Country Lounge Inc.) 99 India St. LIC#LQB-24-26 (ent) 
 
Speaking was Mr. Ralph Garner, 99 India Street, Pawtucket, RI, the applicant. 
Mr. Garner stated that he plans to place four tables near the rear entrance and will operate a 
barbecue in that area through the fall season only. 
The area will be enclosed using Jersey barriers. 
 
There were no other speakers.   The public hearing was closed. 
 
THE CHAIR RECOGNIZED COUNCILOR ARAUJO.   
 
Upon motion made by Councilor Araujo, seconded by Councilor Wildenhain, the following 
petition for expansion of premise was APPROVED on a unanimous voice vote: 
 
CLASS B (VICTUALLER) Expansion of premise to include outdoor seating - 
 
Pawtucket Patriot Bar & Grill (Country Lounge Inc.) 99 India St. LIC#LQB-24-26 (ent) 
 
  
Communication from Ralph Garner president of Pawtucket Patriot Bar and Grill (Country 
Lounge Inc.), 99 In dia Street, to Pawtucket Board of License Commissioners. (Requesting 
name change from Pawtucket Patriot Bar and Grill to Pawtucket Patriot Bar & BBQ) was 
READ AND ORDERED FILED AND THE DBA NAME CHANGE WAS APPROVED ON  
A UNANIMOUS VOICE VOTE. 
 
 
 
THE FOLLOWIN G PUBLIC HEARING  WAS CONTINUED AND APPLICATION FOR 
LICENSE WAS POSTPONED UNTIL THE MEETING ON SEPTEMBER 10, 2026,  ON A 
UNANIMOUS VOICE VOTE: 
 
AUTO REPAIR SHOP New – 
 
Correia Auto Repair (Professional Auto Repair LLC) 102 Esten Avenue, LIC#AUT-26-8® 
(Prev. Woodlawn Village) 
 
 
 
THE UPDATE FOR THE FOLLOWING LICENSE , ORIGINALLY SCHEDULED FOR 
AUGUST 5, 2026, WAS RESCHEDULED TO SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 ON A 
UNANIMOUS VOICE VOTE: 
 
AUTOMOBILE REPAIR SHOP AND SECOND-HAND SHOP LICENSES (CLASS A & B) 
(Selling used automobiles and parts)  
 
*Tiki’s Auto Sales Annex (RZG Inc.) 772 Main St. LIC#AUT-24-68 
Stipulations: 
1. No mechanical repairs in the front of the building. 
2. No debris in the back. 
3. All work must be done inside the building. 
4. All vehicles in the front are for sale only. 01/23/2013
360 
Pawtucket Board of License Commissioners 
August 5, 2026 
 
THE FORMAL HEARING FOR THE FOLLOWING LICENSE , ORIGINALLY 
SCHEDULED FOR AUGUST 5, 2026, WAS RESCHEDULED TO SEPTEMBER 10, 2026, 
ON A UNANIMOUS VOICE VOTE: 
  
KENNEL Renewal - 
 
Harmony (Harmony Dog Training LLC) 65 Patterson Ave. LIC#KNL-25-2 
 
 
THE FOLLOWING PETITION FOR RENEWAL WAS POSTPONED AT THE 
MEETINGS HELD APRIL 8, MAY 6, JUNE 10, AND JULY 8, 2026, AND WAS AGAIN 
POSTPONED UNTIL SEPTEMBER 10, 2026, ON A UNANIMOUS VOICE VOTE: 
 
KENNEL Renewal - 
 
Harmony (Harmony Dog Training LLC) 65 Patterson Ave. LIC#KNL-25-2 
 
 
 
A FORMAL HEARING ON THE FOLLOWING LICENSES WAS TAKEN UP: 
 
CLASS B (VICTUALLER) –  
 
Mangos Hookah Lounge (Princess Investments LLC) 17 Exchange St. LIC#LQB-24-53 
 
Representing the City of Pawtucket was Frank J. Milos, Jr., Esq., City Solicitor. 
 
Mr. Milos stated that an agreement regarding the disposition of this matter was reached for 
Board consideration. If the Board accepts the nolo plea, there will be no suspension; however, 
a $500.00 fine will be imposed and stayed for a period of 120 days.  If no further issues occur 
during that time, the fine would not need to be paid. 
 
Speaking on behalf of Mangos Hookah Lounge was Alex Quiroz, 126 Edgeworth Avenue, 
Providence, RI, license holder.  Mr. Quiroz was sworn in by City Clerk Richard J. Goldstein. 
 
Mr. Quiroz agreed to the terms but expressed concern that the four -month stay would extend 
beyond the renewal date and may affect the renewal of his license. 
 
Chairman Mercer responded that the length of the stay w ould not affect the renewal of the 
license. 
 
Mr. Quiroz stated that the door was locked to prevent homeless individuals from entering the 
premises. 
 
He further stated that the Fire Department has a key and can access the premises at any time. 
He indicated that he could provide a key to the Police Department as well. 
 
There were no other speakers. The formal hearing was closed. 
 
THE CHAIR RECOGNIZED COUNCILOR CODERRE. 
 
Upon motion made by Councilor Coderre, secon ded by Councilor Moreno, the Council 
ACCEPTED THE PLEA OF NOLO CONTENDRE AND ORDER ED THAT A FINE OF 
$500.00 BE IMPOSED, BUT SHALL BE STAYED FOR A PERIOD OF 120 DAYS, for the 
following three reasons: 
 
1.   On or about June 20, 2026: Operating after hours. ( Violation of R.I. Gen. Laws § 3 -
7.1-1 Authorization of temporary extended service hours). 
 
2.   On or about June 20, 2026:  Entertainment after hours.  (Violation of R.I. Gen. Laws § 
3-7.1-1 Authorization of temporary extended service hours).
361 
Pawtucket Board of License Commissioners 
August 5, 2026 
 
3.   On or about June 20, 2026:  Refusing official’s access to licensed premises (Violation 
of R.I. Gen. Laws § 3-2-6)  
 
 
 
Communication from Steven Knapp, Pawtucket Resident, to the Pawtucket City Clerk’s 
Office.  (Noise Pollution – Event at Picos) was READ AND ORDERED FILED. 
 
 
 
A FORMAL HEARING ON THE FOLLOWING LICENSES WAS TAKEN UP: 
 
CLASS B (VICTUALLER) –  
 
Picos Restaurant & Hookah Lounge (Picos  Restaurant & Lounge LLC) 110 School St. 
LIC#LQB-24-60 
 
Representing the City of Pawtucket was Frank J. Milos, Jr., Esq., City Solicitor. 
 
Mr. Milos stated that an agreement regarding the disposition of this matter was reached for 
Board consideration. A $500.00 fine will be imposed, to be paid within 45 days, alon g with a 
one-day suspension to be served on Friday, August 7, 2026. 
 
Speaking on behalf of Picos Restaurant & Hookah Lounge was George Lough, Esq., of Russo 
& Lough, Attorneys at Law. 
 
Mr. Lough stated that there had been some confusion on the part of the owner and that he will 
follow the required protocols going forward. 
 
Chairman Mercer denied that there was any confusion on this matter. 
 
Also speaking was Oswaldino DaSilva, 71 Meadow Street, Pawtucket, RI., license holder.  
 
He stated that his wife had applied for the licenses. 
 
There were no other speakers. The formal hearing was closed. 
 
THE CHAIR RECOGNIZED COUNCILOR CODERRE. 
 
Upon motion made by Councilor Coderre, seconded by Councilor Wildenhain, the Council 
ACCEPTED THE PLEA OF NOLO CONTENDRE AND OR DERED A FINE IN THE 
AMOUNT OF $500.00 TO BE IMPOSED AND PAID WITHIN 45 DAYS, AND THE 
LICENSE TO BE  SUSPENDED FOR THE P ERIOD OF ONE (1) DAY, SPECIFICALLY 
FRIDAY, AUGUST 7, 2026, for the following reasons: 
 
1. On or about July 11, 2026: Expansion of Premise wit hout Board Approval in violation of 
R.I. Gen. Law § 3 -5-17, failure to prohibit the consumption of alcoholic beverages outside of 
the licensed premises and in violation of R.I. Gen. Laws § 3 -5-9, and Rule 1.4.27 of the RI 
Department of Business Regulations  230-RICR-30-10-1 Liquor Control Administration 
“Premises - Retail”, for the sale, service or storage of alcoholic beverages outside the 
established licensed premises without Board approval.  (See attached reports)  
 
2. On or about July 11, 2026: Having a fes tival, show, exhibition or other entertainment 
outside of your licensed premise without first obtaining a license from the City Council in 
violation of Chapter 193 of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Pawtucket.  (See attached 
reports) 
 
 
Communication from Sgt. Jason Lafond , Pawtucket Police Department, to Captain David 
Dolan, and Major Robert Pickett, Pawtucket Police Department.  (Police Response to Large 
Disorderly Crowd at 249 Main Street) was READ AND ORDERED FILED.
362 
Pawtucket Board of License Commissioners 
August 5, 2026 
 
THE CHAIR RECOGNIZED COUNCILOR CODERRE. 
 
With majority consent of the Board, the following motion made by Councilor Coderre, 
seconded by Councilor Wildenhain, was PASSED on a unanimous voice vote: 
 
The Clerk was instructed to issue a summons to Acruz Events and Art Gallery (Acruz Events 
and Art Gallery LLC) 29 Main Street, to appear at a FORMAL HEARING on Thursday, 
September 10, 2026, for the following reason: 
 
1. On or about July 17, 2026:  Failure to maintain control of patron s and/or 
employees, agents; and/or endangering the health, safety and welfare of the 
general public; and/or permitting the house or place where you are licensed to sell 
beverages under the provisions of Title 3 of the General Laws to become 
disorderly as t o annoy and disturb the persons inhabiting or residing in the 
neighborhood; and/or permitting any of the laws of this state or ordinances of this 
city to be violated. (Violation of R.I. Gen. Laws § 3-5-23). 
 
 
  
 
Upon motion made by Councilor Araujo, seconded by Councilor Coderre, the meeting 
was adjourned at 7:43 p.m.
